key_insight: Larger rollout batches can make reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards learn more slowly per unit time, even if they preserve progress per sample. The paper’s “two clocks” view explains why the square-root batch/lr rule can still delay or align collapse and failure on schedule in multi-step training.
problem_solved: The paper addresses how to scale rollout batch size and learning rate in RLVR when model-generated responses are expensive. It explains the gap between theoretical progress-per-sample rules and practical multi-step training behavior, including slower learning and eventual collapse.
method: Introduces a two-clock framework that separates "progress time" from "collapse time" in RLVR training.
Analyzes training under a local quadratic approximation to understand how batch size and learning-rate scaling affect learning dynamics.
Uses the framework to interpret why square-root scaling can look stable in sample efficiency while still changing the wall-clock pace of learning and failure.
impact: For practitioners, this provides a clearer rulebook for choosing batch sizes and learning rates in costly RLVR setups. It helps anticipate when larger batches will slow learning and when training may fail, improving scheduling, stability planning, and compute budgeting.

paper_title: Two Clocks: Why Larger Rollout Batches Learn Slower but Fail on Schedule in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
paper_authors: Yuante Li, Junwei Quan, Kai Qiu, Kate Zhang, Yicheng Tao
